findings.evidence: drain reads peer stdout/stderr into local bytearrays. Timeout/incomplete EOF, the65536-byte check, read error or polling failure raises before return. The files term/kill.stdout and .stderr are created only after drain returns successfully. The exception record saves type/reason/PIDs but not already received bytes, prefix hashes, per-stream counts or observed EOF/exit states. A bootstrap/read failure can therefore lose actual diagnostic bytes while started/failure files exist.
findings.minimumCorrection: In a separately authorized successor, retain each actual chunk incrementally to exclusive per-role stdout/stderr files before checking capacity or throwing. Preserve the crossing chunk and actual received counts/EOF/exit/partial-prefix hash state; keep full hash/stream UNKNOWN when incomplete or killed. Flush/write/hash/cleanup stay under the same native120/115/119 clock and original65536 output acceptance policy; no buffering repair, grace, retry or invented terminal. If a write itself fails, preserve the actual saved file and label unsaved/full state UNKNOWN rather than manufacturing bytes.
findings.scope: New separate availability-only program; no claim that a genuine complete receipt could pass this failure, and no product/helper4 defect. Mask/clock/signals remain UNEXECUTED.
findings.title: Availability drain discards already received partial raw output on failure
